newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes remain firm on July EFP strength.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes remain firm on July EFP strength.

text.p: Cash crude prices in the U.S. Gulf delivered mixed signals Friday morning as July Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) continued to run a healthy premium to July NYMEX futures.

Outright July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was pegged at $21.05-15 a barrel, a shade lower than closing levels Thursday. July NYMEX futures were talked 13-15 cents weaker than benchmark cash WTI, figuring the July EFP value.
July cash WTI also held a premium to August NYMEX values.

July EFPs continue to hold strength on expectations for hefty amounts of foreign crude deliveries against the July NYMEX contract, a trend established for both May and June when more than 2 million barrels of foreigns were delivered each month against paper positions.

"By the fifteenth of June you'll start seeing deliveries of foreign crudes showing in the pipelines to Cushing. That Bonny Light will continued to be passed around until somebody finds a way to run it," said a cash dealer.
Nigerian Bonny Light has been the delivered crude of choice since anyone taking the crude must fork over a 60 cents premium for each barrel.
EFPs gain on this fear of getting stuck with uneconomical foreign supply, allowing EFP buyers to secure WTI matches.
Traders said volumes in the grade markets were modest. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James talked at a slightly weaker 18-13 cents discount to July WTI/Cushing.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was seen at a wide 68-50 cents discount and Midland/WTI steadied at 38-34 cents under.
Sour crudes had West Texas Sour/Midland shading weaker at $1.60-53 under July WTI, and Eugene Island off five cents to a $1.70-58 discount.
July WTI Postings were steady at $1.95-1.98.
July NYMEX prices were rolling with the performance in products, where attention was focused on expiration of June unleaded gasoline and heating oil contracts.
